stem: A client has persistent basophilia on repeated complete blood counts. Which statement by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Basophilia is nonspecific and can occur with hypersensitivity or inflammatory states and with myeloproliferative disorders, so persistent elevation requires clinical evaluation.
options.B: Basophilia is always a benign normal variant and never needs evaluation.
options.C: Basophilia proves an acute bacterial infection.
options.D: Basophilia is diagnostic of a single allergic disorder.

rationale: Basophils participate in immediate hypersensitivity and inflammatory responses. Basophilia is nonspecific and may occur with hypersensitivity or inflammation as well as myeloproliferative neoplasms; persistent basophilia therefore requires interpretation in the full clinical and hematologic context.
educational_objective: Interpret basophilia as a nonspecific finding that may require further evaluation.
source_locator: Clinical significance and etiologies—hypersensitivity/inflammation and myeloproliferative disorders
source_claim_supported: Basophilia can accompany allergic/inflammatory conditions and myeloproliferative disease and is not diagnostic by itself.
correction_summary: Replaced a simplistic cell-function question with a clinically meaningful interpretation of persistent basophilia.
audit_findings: Correct option preserves the broad differential.
Distractors incorrectly make the finding normal or diagnostic.
Independent second pass found one best answer.
